newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Papua relief team find 21 bodies after landslide.
newsitem.headline: Papua relief team find 21 bodies after landslide.

text.p: Papua New Guinea relief workers searching for bodies of 38 people believed to have died in a landslide called off their search on Wednesday because of high winds, a disaster official said.
Twenty-one bodies have been recovered so far.
"High winds have brought the rescue to a halt until tomorrow," the South Pacific nation's director of disaster and emergency services, Leith Anderson, told Reuters.
The landslide buried the remote mountainside village of Waiunda, near Menyamya, early on Sunday after exceptionally heavy monsoon rains.
A total of 38 people are thought to have died in the landslide and eight others were still in hospital in the town of Lae, on the north coast of the PNG mainland, on Wednesday.
Landslides are common in the mountains around the small township of Menyamya because of the combined effects of deforestation and earthquakes.
